data.source_title: Hospital-Based Triage of Obstetric Patients, Committee Opinion No. 667
data.source_setting: Hospital-based obstetric triage; pregnant patients presenting for urgent assessment, including coordination between obstetric units and EDs.
value: Establish hospital-specific triage guidelines collaboratively among obstetric units, emergency departments, ancillary services, and external emergency-response systems.
Use a validated obstetric triage acuity tool as a candidate template to guide prompt evaluation and resource use, adapted to the individual hospital unit.
data.source_evidence_basis: ACOG Committee Opinion 667 explicitly recommends collaboration across obstetric units, EDs, ancillary services, and outside emergency response systems; it says recently developed validated acuity tools may guide quality, efficiency, and resource use and serve as templates for individual units.
data.limitations: This is a systems-level recommendation, not a universal acuity algorithm or fixed timing rule. ACOG states its guidance is not an exclusive course of care and may change; verify current local protocol and current ACOG status before clinical use.
data.inferred_scenario_use: A synthetic triage scenario can model pregnancy-related presentation, acuity assessment, maternal/fetal considerations, and routing among ED, obstetric unit, and ancillary services as locally configured decisions.
data.applicability: Hospital-based triage of obstetric patients; local facility determines location, staffing, timing, and validated acuity tool.
data.source_period: Committee Opinion No. 667, issued July 2016; current reaffirmation/update status is not established by the accessed page (retrieved 2026-10-10).
data.source_n: Not applicable; guideline/pathway, not a patient cohort
data.role_assignment_basis: Role participants are proposed scenario assignments inferred from the pathway setting for simulation design; the cited source does not enumerate this exact role list.
